attempts.summary: Configured a persistent firewalld host firewall on node1 (RHEL 9.8): SSH open to any source, TCP/9000 accepted only from node2 (10.100.66.11) via a rich rule, and TCP/9000 rejected from all other sources (including node3) via a lower-priority reject rich rule. Rules were added --permanent and reloaded, confirmed identical in runtime and permanent config, and firewalld is enabled at boot. Verified functionally: node2→node1:9000 connects and receives data; node3→node1:9000 gets ECONNREFUSED (REJECT); node3→node1:22 connects (SSH open to any address). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured boot_id baselines, issued native systemd reboots that acknowledged before disconnecting, polled until reachable again, confirmed each boot_id changed, and re-verified post-reboot health — node1's firewalld rules persisted through its own reboot and the accept/reject behavior was re-tested and matched pre-reboot results; node2 and node3 came back with active sshd and changed boot identities.
